a.text: Do you know what the cruelest thing in the world is?
Neither total darkness, nor endless torment, nor a dark alley filled with murderers.
It is when a gentle hand pulls you out of a nightmare, just as you thought it was over, and all the pain would come to an end.
Only for you to realize that salvation was just a cruel joke, a brief respite before falling further into the darkness.
Even greater suffering is gazing upon you, within a stone's throw.
And you are powerless before such mockery.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Delphine, do you want to... join us?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The Duke of Windermere's coffin is being transported to the approaching battleships. Some of the refugees have taken it upon themselves to organize a funeral procession, in their gratitude.

a.text: She keeps looking at the place where her mother had fallen, even though any trace of blood is long gone.
It may not be a good idea to invite her now...
I'm already starting to regret it.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Can you thank them for me, Vina? I... I want to stay here a while longer.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: What did they say to you?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Nothing, I'll just stay for a little longer and cool my head.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Swordguards boarded the late-arriving escort fleet. Most of them kept silent while the nobles panicked.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: A moment's weakness, when I tried to help that soldier...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Vampire reached out his hand. Whether it was an obvious trap or not... mother was wounded because of it.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Broken formation and fallen soldiers. Swordguards do not defend their duke. Their only goal is to fulfill their mission—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: —But they faced a foe powerful beyond their imagination.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Delphine...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The staff officers think there was too much personal sentiment in this reckless operation. They never supported it.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: They must believe... that I'm the reason Mother died.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: 'A hero should not die for the weak.'

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: And they're right.

a.text: I gaze at the late-arriving battleships, their standards flying high.
For some reason, I am reminded of Allerdale.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I've cleaned your wounds as best I can, Lady Delphine. This is all I can do with the limited amount of medicine available.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Thank you, doctor.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I must go. The general staff have ordered all troops to report back.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I've left behind some things that belong to you.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: These were the Duke's gifts to you... and you have her sword.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: This may sound impudent, but I hope that you will come back to Irnclad Galavae with us.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Whatever the senior officers say, nothing can change the fact that you are the heir to the title of Duke Windermere.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'll think about it... right now, I just want some quiet.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: How are things?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: They took a bunch of people, but many more remain.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: So, that rough mum really...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Ironic, isn't it? The Duke has trained her officers well.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Even now, the general staff of Windermere continue to plot the next course of action according to the plan.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: What about Delphine?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It seems like the snobbish officers are planning to abandon her.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I don't know. I'm even worried what they might do to Delphine as the 'heir'.

a.text: Heir.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: She... she's not ready.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Duke Windermere was a strong leader. Her Swordguards, her general staff, they all serve the greater good of Victoria alone.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: But she herself...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: She made an admirable, but reckless decision, for the sake of her daughter.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: That decision saved a bunch of lives, though, didnnit?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I'm not criticizing her! I respect her!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: But it means that Delphine is being abandoned by what her mother, Duke Windermere, built on her own.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: What do we do now?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: They took some of the refugees. Can we really trust them? Do we follow the tails of the nobles in the coming battle?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: They didn't take everyone?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: That's not right. If this one ship could take everyone, there's no reason that so many battleships couldn't—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: What's that movement? I thought the ship's engines were out.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: The window!

a.text: Dust rises from the escort fleet that has only just rendezvoused with us.
They're sailing away.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Delphine!

a.text: She stands on the deck, where her mother left this world, holding her mother's sword in her arms, as she did before I went below.
The wind sweeps at her short hair. Her solitude makes her look even smaller than she is.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: What's going on—

a.text: I grab her shoulder. Only then does she come out of her stupor.
I see none of the anger, fear, or sorrow that I expected to see. She's wearing barely any emotion at all.
Only calm, flat disappointment, and a quiet so deep it is painful to see.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: They're gone.

a.text: Her voice trembles a little.
But it's still too calm.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: There are civilians down below waiting to see the Duke of Windermere's coffin off!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Those bastards didn't mind running innocent people over?!

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: What's going on?!

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: That's wasn't part of the orders! Maybe there was a miscommunication...

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: We still have a few good IFVs. We need to head back to Irnclad Galavae and get confirmation!

a.text: Pah.
I've never gazed upon the tail of a battleship so intently.
How ridiculous.
The marks that the rain of blood left on our clothes is a lingering reminder of that cruel attack.
Several hours have passed since we left the Duke of Windermere's flagship.
Bad news keeps coming. We did a head count as we left the ship. The Doctor, Amiya and Ascalon were not there.
We only had time to do a brief search, which came up empty.
All I can do is keep faith in their strength. But for some reason, I think back to Amiya's lean shoulders.
Sorrow and helplessness are luxuries that this group can no longer afford.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Stop dawdling!

steps.name: Norport Refugee
steps.text: I... I really can't go any further...

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I'll whip you if I have to!

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Get up! Stay with the armor if you want to live!

steps.name: Norport Refugee
steps.text: I... I need to catch my breath, sir... I have a condition...

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: No dawdling. This isn't just about your life—

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Hands off, Norport hoodlum. I'm just carrying out my orders.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: They're not trained soldiers. They've been at a forced march for five straight hours. They don't have any strength left.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Then they can lie down and die.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: We're trying to save their lives! Everything can still be salvaged, if we make it back to Irnclad Galavae.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: They need to stop and rest.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I said—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's not just for them. It's for you too, Ensign. I know your condition.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Not many soldiers were left behind, but I know almost all of you are Infected—

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Shut up!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'll let that slide... this once.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You're Duke Windermere's man. Do not let your actions defile her memory.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I—

a.text: Infection, a curse they fear more than any other.
Catch up to the ship that abandoned them. Hide the growing black crystals under the bandage.
Fool yourself.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I'm sorry... It's just, don't say that blasted word!

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I'm fine... I'm fine!

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I said to keep a low profile on the barrens and avoid drawing Sarkaz attention.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Sir, I...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's getting dark. The civilians trying to keep up with you need to rest, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: No. We continue the march as planned.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: We can reach Hill 31 by midnight at our current pace.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: We'll reestablish communication with Irnclad Galavae there. Only once we're in touch with the nomadic fortress are we truly safe.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: If we wait until morning, I doubt this group is ready to face the Sarkaz and—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You're the ranking officer and de facto commander here, and the ship's doctor.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You know as well as I do that we're trying to catch a fast battleship with our own feet and a few tanks.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I respect your decision, Lieutenant, but we don't even know why those battleships left.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If they didn't respond to your hails at the time, why do you think the fortress will open its gates to us?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I checked on the group. We have less than three companies of combat-effective soldiers, and nearly a thousand refugees following in tow.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: By the time the march that you had in mind is done, there will be less than twenty percent left.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Vina, right? Listen—

a.text: He avoids my gaze.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I mean twenty percent of your soldiers.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: And none of the refugees.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Sir... (whisper)

a.text: I need not hear what they're saying. I saw what happened.
Someone bled his last in the long, silent wall of people.
He left behind a long trail of blood, mixed in with the mud.
The Lieutenant's silence hardly lasts two breaths.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Slow down a little...

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: We'll keep going—

a.text: Idiot.
My fist leaves its mark on his face.
I heard a crisp sound. I think I dislocated his jaw.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: ...Argh...

a.text: He quickly puts his jaw back in place. Must have dealt with this sort of thing a lot.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: You assaulted a soldier, hooligan.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I could have you executed, according to Victorian Service Law.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Stand up.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You could try to execute me. Or we can keep going.

a.text: The fist is a solution that can only be used once in a while.
Dagda, Morgan, and Indra stand in front of the soldiers on edge.
The civilians surround us silently.
It reminds me of how we used to fight turf wars on the streets.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Stand down! Do NOT open fire!

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: They called you Siege, didn't they? They were telling stories that you're actually highborn or something, and with that accent...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'm a hooligan... leader of the Glasgow Gang.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Fine, I don't care. Listen, I'm a soldier who has pledged his loyalty to the Duke of Windermere...

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: My duty is to fulfill the mission handed down by my commander!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'm waiting for you to wipe the blood from your mouth.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Give up. Your elbow is about to dislocate.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Some... sacrifices are acceptable in order to protect the many.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: And just who are the many?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Have you taken a good look at who you're leading?!

a.text: Frightened soldiers, silent civilians, the Infected, the wounded.
The people standing around us.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'd had enough.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I want to tell them, those who escaped hell in Norport...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'm still looking out for them. There's still someone who cares about them.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Might makes right. Law of the streets, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'm telling you now that they're going to make camp here, and they're going to rest. We must reconsider our course of action.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: If we're cut off from the main force at Irnclad Galavae, everyone is going to die when we run into the Sarkaz. Every last one—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Enough.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Don't insult the memory of the Duke of Windermere any more, Lieutenant Shearer, if you still think you're part of her army.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: How could you—

a.text: Delphine clutches the hilt of her sword.
It surprises me. Even more than it surprises Lieutenant Shearer. He's surprised, and angry.
I'm suddenly reminded that he had provided medical aid to everyone on the ship, before Irnclad Galavae abandoned us.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Delphine. Your clothes, and the sword...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: A little big for me, is it?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But I need you all to hear me out.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Is the Lieutenant leaving?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Yes. They formed a small squad and picked the tank in best condition. He can leave at any time.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: That squad will travel light and quick. They can reach the marked location before dawn.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You put those clothes on.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Maybe what they represent still means something to someone.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I've spoken to my troops, Lady Delphine. They will follow your orders until I return.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: For the last time, my lady, you're the heir to Windermere. No matter what happens, you should come with us—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Sorry, but I must stay.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: This was my promise to the people. They need to know that Victoria has not abandoned them.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: They need this hope to keep going... we can only trust each other now. We must trust each other.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: If the departure of the escorts was just a misunderstanding or a mutiny by a few, then Irnclad Galavae will welcome us, whether I'm there or not.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: And if not...

a.text: The Lieutenant's eyelid twitches. Delphine's words are certainly subversive.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: My presence will only make things worse. At least you'll live.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: My lady! It's not my own hide that I'm concerned—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: They let me go the first time, perhaps out of respect for my mother, perhaps out of a sense of... pity. But they won't give me a second chance.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I trust my comrades, and the officers' loyalty to the Duke.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Please take this locating beacon, Lady Delphine. I promise to bring back good news.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: As for you...

a.text: The man gazes calmly at me. I clench my fist, preparing for a sucker punch.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: ...You've got some hard knuckles. Take care of Lady Delphine.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Cheers, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Siege, we checked up on the refugees from Norport.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Perhaps the Duke of Windermere had given orders behind our backs... things were chaotic when we boarded the ship, and we couldn't find the one who executed the order.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Regardless, their screening was impeccable. There is no sign of Infection amongst the refugees in the group.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: But now...

a.text: I look in the direction where the Lieutenant departed.
Of course.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Many soldiers who fought amidst Sarkaz witchcraft are showing acute Infection symptoms.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: These soldiers got Oripathy fighting the Sarkaz. How could their comrades just abandon them like that?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It's an old military tradition. And not a strictly Victorian one; it's the same in Kazimierz, Ursus, Gaul.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Infected are not allowed in camps. More conscientious commanders might put the Infected in their own unit, and send them on the most dangerous missions.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But for the military, there's far too much uncertainty in the Infected and their uncontrolled Arts.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Some must have resisted.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: No one ever succeeded. Looking back on history, the Infected make up a relatively small portion of armies in times of war. Acceptable losses in exchange for stability on the front lines.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It's even in the textbooks of the Royal Military Academy.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It's just—
'The honorable martyrs who died for the glorious foundation.'

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Now, now, no need to get violent, ladies.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I'm here to talk.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: First, let me make clear that the death of Her Grace Duke Windermere has nothing to do with the part of Victoria that I serve.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: In fact, I bring my sincerest condolences, Lady Delphine. My own position aside, I believe she glowed brighter than any hero in the Battle of the Four Emperors.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But now, who will fill the gap that her death leaves behind? Who can step up to take her place in the grand strategic theater?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Duke Wellington is an accomplished soldier, but we all know he has no intention of giving his all.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Duke Caster has her hands full coordinating everything. Frankly, the death of Duke Windermere is a big, big problem.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You sure got the news quickly, didn't you?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Well, it's my business to know. You'd be familiar... with our line of work.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: What are you here for?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I suggest you think carefully about the next words coming out of your mouth.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Flowers for the hero, Lady Windermere, and a gift of rations and ammunition.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: In exchange for?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You know full well, Your Royal Highness.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The scrap of metal known as the Sighs of Kings.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: To be honest, I have no use for this sword, personally.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You want to trade, sure.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: My conditions are simple—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Take that damnable Stone of the Sword of yours, and bring it to the front lines, where the storm blows the fiercest, where fire falls the hardest.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You can get lost if your plan is to keep this sword safely in the rear, to prop up a tent for kings and nobles to drink tea beneath.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If you really will bring this thing to the lines, and provide shelter for Victoria's warriors, citizens, and the poor souls who have lost their homes...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If it is a shelter for all, whether the son of a blacksmith or the daughter of a teacher, whether they take pay in the name of Victoria or carry weapons of their own making...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Then, by all means, you can have this piece of metal.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Come to me with the Stone of the Sword, Trilby Asher. I promise that I will never fall behind you on the front lines, not by a single step.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Oh my.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: This is beyond my discretion. I'm just an envoy, after all. Her Grace the Duke of Caster has the final decision.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Then go to your master. Come back to me once you have an answer from my dear aunt.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I'll do my best, Your Royal Highness Alexandrina.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But... this is just a promise on a personal level.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: What follows now is off the record. Some personal opinions, not of Trilby Asher, but of Sir Suffolk, Bellingham.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: A new voice is not necessarily a bad thing.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You've taken in Infected soldiers... well, and many more civilians, but the point stands... that's all good and fine. But it's not enough. You need an army. Your own army.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: An army with a place for them.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You...

a.text: I'm surprised. Perhaps it's a Caster trick...
But he is encouraging me to form my own Reunion.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Looks like you really did turn off your sound recorder.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Can't do it for too long. Colleagues start getting suspicious, you know.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: ...My grandmother was executed after getting Infected in the War of the Four Nations.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: When she left, she told me with a laugh that there was less than a three percent chance of getting Oripathy in battle. It was only when I inherited the title and looked through the records in the archives that I learned...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: The three percent figure has been in use for centuries.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: It has never changed, even though we're using more Originium machines and more complex Originium Arts in modern warfare.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Perhaps you haven't noticed because all you can see is a small corner of the battlefield. Certainly the dukes haven't noticed, because they have their sights set way too far away. But I have.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: The Infection problem in the Victorian Army is serious. Serious on an unprecedented scale.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Everyone exercises restraint in a conflict between 'civilized' nations.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: No one wants their camp to be filled with ticking, living time bombs, or seize a dirty city covered in Originium dust.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But now... our enemy is the Sarkaz.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: If you really mean to do this, Siege, then it has the potential to be a good thing for your reputation, for my career... perhaps, even for our country.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Thanks for the concern, but my friends and I know the Infected better than you do. We'll be fine.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Oh, by the way, I have some scrap equipment here that nobody wants or cares about. Leftovers, you know.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You can have them. It's all trash, after all.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Farewell, then.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: How much do you believe him?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I would rather believe that even someone like him could not stay out of this conflict.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: What did he leave behind? A recording and coordinates?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This sound—

a.text: 'Bzzzz—'
'Need... support... Chetleigh...'
'Surrounded... Tempest Platoon...'
'Requesting aid!'
